Student support prioritisation: research demonstration

A research demo of how a dropout-risk model could help staff decide whom to offer support after the first semester. Public data (UCI, Portugal); not for real decisions.

543 of 4,424 students showni · ← → keys move between students
How to read this page (first time? start here)
  1. Pick a student with the list, the arrows, or an example. Each is a real but anonymous record from the public dataset.
  2. Section 1 says whether the model would put this student on the support-contact list. Staff can contact only about 1 in 5 students, so the model ranks everyone and flags the top 20%.
  3. Section 2 shows which information pushed the model's estimate up or down for this student.
  4. Section 3 shows how much to trust that list of reasons: the same calculation was repeated 10 times with small changes.
  5. Section 4 asks whether clearing a fee or debt record would change the flag. Section 5 lets you try your own changes (only when started with --what-if).

Terms: estimate = the model's dropout probability, a score rather than a certainty. Rank = position from highest to lowest estimate among the 544. Flagged = in the top 108 (20%). Contribution = how much one group of information moved the estimate (SHAP); it shows association, not cause.

Read before acting

  • The flag means "in this cohort's top 20% of estimated risk" (outreach capacity), not a fixed cut-off.
  • A model estimate for adviser review, not a decision or diagnosis. Outreach should be voluntary support.
  • Trained and checked on one Portuguese dataset; not validated for any other institution.
  • Enrolled students (outcome unknown) were excluded from training and this cohort.
